School meals and payments
We use ParentPay to help families and school work together to support everyday school life.ParentPay is a secure online payment system.You can use it to pay for school meals, trips and other school activities online.
Setting up to Parent Pay.
If you have lost the activation letter, contact the school office.If you need help setting up or using ParentPay, please email:
ParentPay setup: finance@furzedownschool.org.uk Meal bookings: torme@furzedownschool.org.uk
Free school meals are also available to pupils in years 3 and above whose parents receive certain benefits. For more information please email: office@furzedownschool.org.uk or download this form: Free school meal form
School uniform helps children feel part of the school community and ready for the day.
We understand that some children may need flexibility with uniform because of sensory or regulation needs. Please contact us if you have any concerns.
These items can be bought from any shop:– White shirt or polo shirt– Black or dark grey trousers, shorts or skirt– Black shoes with a low heel
Children can also wear a blue checked summer dress during warm weather.
Uniform with the school logo:
These can be bought from: PL School Wear
– Sweatshirt– Fleece– Cardigan– Hoody
School coats and bags are also available but are optional.
– Blue logo polo shirt from PL School Wear – Black leggings, joggers or shorts
Post-16 students should wear smart clothes suitable for work or college. For example:– Shirt or blouse– Black trousers– Jacket or blazer– Knee-length skirt– Smart dress– Black low-heel shoes

Progress and Assessment
Understanding Progress
At Furze Down, we recognise that progress looks different for every pupil.
Assessment helps us understand what pupils know, what they can do and what they need to learn next. It allows us to celebrate achievements, identify next steps and ensure learning remains ambitious and personalised.
We assess progress across both parts of our curriculum:
EHCP Developmental Framework
– Communication and Interaction
– Social Emotional Health and Wellbeing
– Physical and Sensory Development
– Preparation for Adulthood
– Cognition and Learning
Progress in academic and vocational learning.
How Do We Assess Progress?
Assessment is an ongoing part of teaching and learning.
Teachers, therapists and support staff gather evidence through observations, discussion, practical activities, classwork and EHCP reviews to build a picture of each pupil's development and progress.
EHCP Outcomes and Short-Term Goals
Every pupil's learning journey is shaped by their EHCP.
Short-term goals are reviewed regularly and help ensure learning remains personalised, meaningful and focused on each pupil's next steps.
Working Together with Families
Progress is shared through Annual Reviews, EHCP reporting, parent consultations and regular communication between home and school.

FURZE DOWN SCHOOL
EHCP Developmental Framework
The EHCP Developmental Framework develops the skills, behaviours and attributes pupils need to flourish in life, learning, work and leisure.
Working alongside the Cognition Framework, it provides a clear structure for supporting personal development and preparing pupils for adulthood.
The framework is organised into five strands.
Strand 1: Communication and Interaction
Developing communication, language and social interaction skills that support learning, relationships and independence.
Strand 2: Social Emotional Health and Wellbeing
Developing self-awareness, emotional regulation, resilience, positive relationships and personal responsibility.
Strand 3: Physical and Sensory Development
Developing physical skills, coordination, body awareness and sensory regulation to support learning, wellbeing and independence.
Strand 4: Preparation for Adulthood
Developing the knowledge, skills and experiences needed for employment, independent living, community participation and healthy lifestyles.
Strand 5: Cognition and Learning
Developing engagement, thinking skills, reflection and independent learning behaviours that support successful learning.
The framework helps teachers, therapists and support staff identify strengths, set meaningful goals and plan learning that is ambitious, personalised and relevant.
Together with the Cognition Framework, it ensures pupils are supported to make meaningful progress towards adulthood and lifelong wellbeing.

FURZE DOWN SCHOOL
Our curriculum provides a framework that prepares pupils for life, learning, work and leisure.
At Furze Down, we recognise that our pupils' developmental stages are often significantly different from those of their mainstream peers. Rather than being based on age, our curriculum is shaped by each child's stage of development.
It has been carefully designed to prepare children and young people for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life.
Our aim is to help every pupil flourish in school, at home, in their communities and in adult life.
We build our curriculum around our pupils' individual needs, not around subject boundaries.
How Our Curriculum Works
Through our EHCP Developmental Framework and Cognition Framework.
When designing our curriculum, we draw on the requirements of both the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and the National Curriculum. These provide important reference points for knowledge, skills and assessment.
However, learning at Furze Down is organised around pupils' developmental needs, EHCP outcomes and preparation for adulthood.
Our curriculum combines two complementary frameworks.
The EHCP Developmental Framework
Matching the school's provision to the outcomes stated in the students EHCPs.
Developing the communication, emotional, physical, sensory and independence skills pupils need to engage successfully in learning and everyday life.
This includes:– Communication and Interaction– Social, Emotional Health and Wellbeing– Physical and Sensory Development– Cognition and Learning– Preparation for Adulthood
The Cognition FrameworkDeveloping knowledge, understanding and skills through academic and vocational learning.
This includes:– English– Mathematics– Science– Humanities– Computing– Creative Arts– Vocational Learning
Together, these frameworks ensure pupils develop both the personal skills and subject knowledge required to thrive.
Preparation for Adulthood
At Furze Down pupils develop the knowledge, skills and independence needed for adulthood.
Preparation for adulthood is a golden thread that runs throughout our curriculum.
Across all phases of the school, pupils develop knowledge, skills and experiences related to employment, independent living, community inclusion and health and wellbeing
Developmental pathways
Pupils access learning through pathways that reflect their developmental stage rather than their chronological age.
This ensures learning is relevant, appropriately challenging and focused on each pupil's next steps.
Building the foundations for communication, learning, relationships, wellbeing and independence.
Developing confidence, independence, subject knowledge and skills for everyday life.
Preparing pupils for greater independence, qualifications, employment and adult life.
Across all pathways, learning is matched to individual strengths, needs and aspirations, helping every pupil make meaningful progress.

FURZE DOWN SCHOOL
The Cognition Framework develops pupils' knowledge, understanding and skills across a broad range of academic and vocational subjects.
Drawing on both the Early Years Foundation Stage and the National Curriculum, it provides learning that is adapted to each pupil's developmental stage and individual needs.
Through exploration, investigation, creativity and real-life experiences, pupils develop an understanding of themselves, their communities and the wider world.
Working alongside the EHCP Developmental Framework, the Cognition Framework helps pupils build the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for life, learning, work and leisure.
The Cognition Framework includes:
– Literacy – reading, writing, composition and transcription.– Mathematics – developing mathematical understanding and applying maths in everyday life.– Understanding the World – project-based learning including science (with Forest School), design and technology, computing, history, geography, religious education and languages.– Creative and Expressive Arts – project-based learning including art and design and music.
Preparation for Adulthood is embedded throughout the curriculum, developing pupils' knowledge and skills in employment, community inclusion and health. Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education are integrated within these areas.
In Key Stage 4 and Sixth Form, pupils also access vocational learning tailored to their interests, strengths and future aspirations.
